Shadhin Bangla Betar Kendra singers inspired nation in 1971
2017-03-19T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/shadhin-bangla-betar-kendra-singers-inspired-nation-1971-1378144

Singers of Shadhin Bangla Betar Kendra (SBBK) had not only played key roles in inspiring the nation in 1971, but also financially assisted Bangladeshi refugees languishing in India, said speakers at a reception accorded to the singers yesterday.

Abdul Jabbar, Apel Mahmud and Namita Ghosh -- three noted singers of the wartime radio station -- reminisced about playing at different places in India's Agartala and giving away the earned money to the Bangladeshi refugees there.

Seven singers of the SBBK were honoured at the ceremony organised by Rotary Club of Metropolitan Dhaka, Ashfaque Nazma Foundation, and Inner Wheel Club of Metropolitan Dhaka, at The Daily Star Centre in the capital.

Four other singers were Rathindranath Roy, Dalia Nausheen, Kaderi Kibria, and Shaheen Samad.

The singers were presented with crest, garland, sash and gifts.

They performed signature track “Tir Hara Ei Dheu-er Sagor Pari Debo Rey” in chorus.

“You inspired the nation through your patriotic songs that also boosted the morale of our freedom fighters,” said Tawfiq Ali, president of the Rotary Club of Metropolitan Dhaka.

Abdul Jabbar said many singers and staff of SBBK were yet to be recognised despite their contribution to the country's liberation.

“Some of them are even struggling to make ends meet for years,” he said, urging the government to provide them with financial support.
